cur:catacombs2-zaragoza-petrine-trilogy.summary: The left part of this frieze is given to three scenes of Peter: the miracle of the spring, his arrest, and Christ foretelling his denial as the cockerel stands by. A praying woman, the orant, occupies the centre; to the right Christ heals a blind man, changes water into wine at Cana, multiplies the loaves and fishes and, at the far end, raises Lazarus from his tomb.
facts: The three Peter scenes on the left gave the sarcophagus its modern name, the 'Petrine trilogy'.
Spanish Wikipedia attributes it to the Roman workshop that produced the Sarcophagus of the Two Brothers in the Vatican.
Only the front is carved; it was restored in 1991.

cur:objects3-drumcliff-high-cross.summary: The head of the high cross at Drumcliff, on the site of a monastery founded by St Columba, is carved with a standing figure of Christ at the crossing, usually identified as Christ in Glory, with small figures on the arms and a panel of Daniel below. The other face of the cross turns to the Gospel: the Arrest or Mocking of Christ between two soldiers and, higher up, the Crucifixion with Stephaton offering the vinegar and Longinus raising his spear. It is the only surviving high cross of its kind in County Sligo.
facts: The cross is said to bear the only known representation of the Virgin and Child on any Irish high cross, on the side of one arm.
Its scheme gives unusual prominence to the infancy of John the Baptist, a figure much honoured in the Columban monastic tradition.
High-relief animals, including a camel on one face and a lion on the other, stride across the shaft between the scriptural panels.
cur:objects3-drumcliff-high-cross.notes: Dating is uncertain: the Drumcliff Monastery article gives a tentative 9th or 10th century on artistic grounds, while the Drumcliff article dates the cross to c. 1100. The identification of the head figure as Christ in Glory follows the photographer's caption; many scenes on this cross are debated.
